tools.name: read_session_channel
tools.title: Read Session Channel
tools.description: Read records from a session's realtime stream: a named side channel (pass `channel`) or the reserved chat transcript pair (omit `channel`). By default returns whatever records exist after the optional cursor and closes (a point-in-time drain). Set `timeoutInSeconds` to wait for the next record when none exist yet. Read `out` for the producer's feed (e.g. a screencast) or `in` for what clients have sent. Use the returned nextCursor as `afterEventId` to page forward.

sessionId.description: The session id (session_* friendlyId) or the externalId it was created with.

channel.description: The named side channel to read. Omit to read the session's reserved chat transcript pair.

io.description: Which side to read: `out` (producer feed) or `in` (client input).

afterEventId.description: Cursor: only return records after this event id. Use the nextCursor from a prior read.

timeoutInSeconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for at least one record when none exist yet (a bounded tail). Omit for an immediate point-in-time read.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.title: Submit Feedback
tools.description: Report a problem with the Trigger.dev MCP server, SDK, or documentation. Use this when a tool returned a confusing error, the docs disagreed with the actual behaviour, a capability you needed was missing, or you had to work around something to finish the user's task. Describe what you were trying to do, what happened, and what you expected instead, in your own words. Never include secrets, credentials, environment variables, tokens or the user's own data - summarise and redact instead of pasting raw output. Tell the user what you reported. Do not call this more than once for the same problem.

message.description: What you were trying to do, what actually happened, and what you expected instead, in your own words. Summarise the failing call and error rather than pasting raw output, and leave out secrets, credentials, environment variables and the user's own data.

toolName.description: The MCP tool the problem happened in, if it was one tool in particular.

tools.name: replay_run
tools.title: Replay Run
tools.description: Replay a run: create a new run of the same task in the same environment, reusing the original run's payload, metadata, tags, queue, concurrency key and machine. Pass any of payload, metadata, tags, queue, concurrencyKey, machine, version, region, delay, ttl, idempotencyKey, maxAttempts, maxDuration or priority to override them for the new run. The run ID starts with run_

projectRef.description: The trigger.dev project ref, starts with proj_. We will attempt to automatically detect the project ref if running inside a directory that includes a trigger.config.ts file, or if you pass the --project-ref option to the MCP server.

runId.description: The ID of the run to get the details of, starts with run_

payload.description: A new payload for the replayed run, as the actual payload object (not a JSON string). Omit it to reuse the original run's payload.

metadata.description: New metadata for the replayed run. Omit it to reuse the original run's metadata.

tags.description: Tags for the replayed run, replacing the original run's tags. Up to 10.

queue.description: The name of an existing queue to run on. Omit it to use the original run's queue.

concurrencyKey.description: The concurrency key for the replayed run

machine.description: The machine preset for the replayed run

version.description: Lock the replayed run to this deployed version, e.g. 20250101.1. Defaults to the current version.

region.description: The region to run in. Defaults to the original run's region.

delay.description: Delay the replayed run, as a duration like 1h30m or an ISO 8601 date

ttl.description: How long the replayed run can stay queued before it expires, as a duration like 10m or a number of seconds

idempotencyKey.description: An idempotency key for the replayed run

maxAttempts.description: The maximum number of attempts for the replayed run

maxDuration.description: The maximum duration in seconds of the replayed run

priority.description: Priority offset in seconds. Higher values are dequeued sooner.

tools.name: write_session_channel
tools.title: Write Session Channel
tools.description: Append one record to a named side channel's `in` stream on a session. Use this to send control input to a running agent (e.g. a pause/viewport command) without waking or triggering a run. Requires a `channel` name; the reserved transcript and the `out` side are not writable here (`out` is producer-only). Pass `value` as an object for a structured record or a string for a raw one.

tools.name: replay_webhook_delivery
tools.title: Replay Webhook Delivery
tools.description: Replay a webhook delivery from its stored event as a new delivery. With no targetId it goes to every subscriber again, re-checking their filters; with targetId it goes to that one subscriber even if its filter skipped the event. Replays trigger real runs, so confirm with the user first.

tools.name: generate_webhook_secret
tools.title: Generate Webhook Secret
tools.description: Generate a new signing secret for a hosted webhook endpoint and return it once, for providers where you choose the secret (for example GitHub). It replaces the existing secret; pass previousSecretTtlSeconds to keep accepting the old one while you update the provider, otherwise deliveries signed with it fail. Never print, log or commit the returned secret. The returned secret enters your context. To keep it out, run the CLI instead: `npx trigger.dev@latest webhooks generate-secret <endpoint> --env <env> --to-env <NAME>` saves it to .env.local without printing it, so you can pass it to the provider by variable name, or `--print` pipes it straight into the provider's CLI. When the endpoint already has a secret, add `--previous-secret-ttl` (for example 24h, or 0 if the old secret leaked). Prefer the CLI whenever you can run shell commands.

branch.description: The branch to get tasks for, only used for preview environments and branchable development environments

endpointId.description: The webhook endpoint: its declared id (e.g. payments) or wh_ id. Use list_webhook_endpoints to find it.

previousSecretTtlSeconds.description: Keep accepting the replaced secret for this many seconds (at most 604800, 7 days) so deliveries the provider still signs with it keep verifying. Omit or pass 0 to replace it immediately, for example when it leaked.

tools.name: set_webhook_secret
tools.title: Set Webhook Secret
tools.description: Store the signing secret (or public key) a provider issued for a hosted webhook endpoint, for example the whsec_ secret Stripe returns when a webhook endpoint is created. It replaces the existing secret; pass previousSecretTtlSeconds to keep accepting the old one for a while. The secret you pass here enters your context. To keep it out, run the CLI instead, which never prints it: pipe it from the provider's CLI (`<provider command> | npx trigger.dev@latest webhooks set-secret <endpoint> --env <env>`), or read it from an environment variable or the project's .env files (`webhooks set-secret <endpoint> --env <env> --from-env STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). When the endpoint already has a secret, add `--previous-secret-ttl` (for example 24h, or 0 if the old secret leaked). Prefer the CLI whenever you can run shell commands.
